metadata.note: Winston-Salem Southbound Railway (organized 1905; jointly owned by the Norfolk and Western and the Atlantic Coast Line, now by Norfolk Southern and CSX), Winston-Salem - Lexington - High Rock - Whitney - Albemarle - Norwood - Wadesboro, about 90 mi. Passenger service 24 Nov 1910 (inaugural; regular from 17 Dec 1910 to Whitney, 13 Feb 1911 to Albemarle, 3 Mar 1911 to Wadesboro) to 8 Jul 1933, a mixed train only from mid-1932; freight only since (not drawn, Rule 1). Drawn: Winston-Salem - Whitney 1910-1933, Whitney - Wadesboro 1911-1933, and the Whitney - Badin shuttle 1917-1924 with both ends [OPEN]. The WSSB ran its own trains throughout, so no Rule 4 split; the colour is new to the dataset (no other company uses #6443BF). The Wadesboro - Florence through service over the ACL (from 1 May 1911) belongs to the ACL layer and is not drawn here. The HPT&D (High Point - High Rock) is a separate layer.
sources: NC Corporation Commission, Report 1931-32 (archive.org reportofcorporat1932nort): Docket 7181 pp.45-46, express-office order No. 7346, annual return pp.173-174
NC Corporation Commission, Report 1933-34 (reportofcorporat1934nort) return pp.197-198; Report 1929-30 (reportofcorporat1930nort) pp.328-329 and Yadkin RR road-operated table
NC Utilities Commission, Report 1938 (reportofutilitie1938nort) Southmont agency order pp.314-316
Jeff Miller & Jim Vaughn, 'The Winston-Salem Southbound Railway' (read second-hand through frograil and wvncrails; not consulted directly)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py on 2026-11-05. The WSSB is live track (Norfolk Southern / CSX jointly) and OSM tags it name/operator='Winston-Salem Southbound Railway' with old_railway_operator='joint (ACL/N&W)' (the latter shared with the HPT&D, so the trace was checked vertex by vertex against the WSSB-named ways: every vertex lies within 40 m of one).
metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) [OPEN] Whitney - Badin shuttle: drawn 1917-1924, both ends open - 1917 is the first confirmed year (a 1916 joint-operation contract is reported but unread; NCC 1916-1918 reports annualreportofco1916nort / reportofcorporat1918nort may print it) and 1924 the last confirmed year; the end is bounded only by 8 Jul 1933. Whether the Yadkin also ran Badin passenger trains is unknown. (2) Possible 1934 conflict: the NC Utilities Commission 1936 report's 1934 statistics table may show 150 WSSB passengers (OCR column alignment garbled); against it stand the 8 Jul 1933 end (Miller & Vaughn), the June 1933 grant and 'discontinued a few years ago' (1938). 1933 is drawn; the page image (reportofutilitie1936nort ~p.290) is unchecked. (3) wvncrails says the ACL 'supervised exclusively' the WSSB c.1910-1912; read as management, not ACL-operated trains - if trains ran as ACL trains this would be a Rule 4 split. (4) Inaugural date 24 vs 25 Nov 1910 (same year either way). (5) Hearne (Fowler 'b pass?'): passenger stop or not. (6) Train counts other than 1917 and 1932-33 are not established, so the 1910-1931 headway is an estimate. (7) Geometry: the pre-1927 alignment at High Rock Lake and the pre-1926 Winston-Salem terminal approach (first union station) are not drawn - see geometry_quality.

properties.geometry_quality: Winston-Salem - Whitney: traced 47.3 mi (46.8 mi on WSSB-tagged ways, 0.5 mi untagged yard/connecting track) against a documented 48.6 mi (Fowler milepost for Whitney, 0.0 at Winston-Salem Union Station) - 2.7% short. No approximated (straight-line) legs. Waypoints: the 1926 Union Station approach (hand-pinned; trace starts on WSSB track 0.3 km SSW of the station building), Lexington (Nominatim town, 1.1 km from the line), Southmont (hamlet, 0.1 km), the HPT&D junction at High Rock (hand-pinned; Nominatim returned High Rock peak in Madison County), Whitney (hamlet, 0.0 km); Tuckertown (returned the reservoir) and Eller (returned a Buncombe County stream) were not used. LATER-ALIGNMENT FLAGS (Rule 2): (1) WINSTON-SALEM TERMINAL - the line is drawn to the second union passenger station, opened 1926; per Fowler the first union station, used 1910-1925, was about 1 mi different in milepost and its approach is not drawn; the 1910 inaugural train left from the N&W freight depot, also not drawn. The Southern's trackage beyond the station approach is deliberately not drawn. (2) HIGH ROCK LAKE - the line between Southmont and the Yadkin crossing at High Rock dam is drawn on the present alignment, which crosses the lake (impounded 1927) on a long fill and crosses the river immediately below the 1927 dam; the 1910-1927 valley-floor alignment probably differed but neither OSM (abandoned/historic ways) nor OpenHistoricalMap has any record of it, so 1910-1926 is drawn on a probably later (c.1927) alignment, unverified. The river crossing below the dam now lies in Tuckertown Reservoir (impounded 1962), so that bridge may also post-date the passenger era.

segments.note: Winston-Salem Southbound passenger trains, Winston-Salem (Southern's union passenger station, by trackage rights) - South Winston-Salem - Welcome - Lexington - Southmont - High Rock - Tuckertown - Whitney. Inaugural run Thanksgiving Day 24 Nov 1910 (golden spike 23 Nov; SNAP gives 25 Nov - sources differ by a day, both 1910): N&W 4-4-0 #519 and coach #957 left the N&W freight depot at 12:35 pm and reached Wadesboro about 7 pm. Regular scheduled Winston-Salem - Whitney service began 17 Dec 1910 (wvncrails after Miller & Vaughn). WSSB ran its own trains with its own crews and power throughout (jointly owned by the N&W and ACL; wvncrails says the ACL 'supervised exclusively' for the first two years, read as management, not ACL-operated trains - see not_yet_sourced). In 1917 there were 4 trains a day the length of the line plus the Badin shuttles; riders 24,638 in 1911, 151,294 in 1917, then a steep decline (17,978 revenue passengers in 1928, 10,387 in 1930, 7,503 in 1931). headway_min 720 is an estimate (Rule 3) from the 1917 count of 4 through trains a day (2 each way); the number of trains in other years was not established. This segment ends at 1931 because from mid-1932 only a mixed train ran (next segment).
sources: Segment-level: start 1910 (inaugural run 24 Nov 1910, regular service from 17 Dec 1910) from Winston-Salem Time Traveler and wvncrails (after Miller & Vaughn); 1917 train count and ridership from frograil after Miller & Vaughn; 1928-1931 ridership from the NCC annual returns - as quoted in research/branches/winston_salem_southbound_railway.txt (researched 2026-11-05); the tracer did not re-open these pages. Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Winston-Salem - Whitney: the last passenger years. End: the Corporation Commission's Docket 7181 order (hearing and order 28 Jul 1932) refused abandonment but let the road replace its passenger trains with 'a mixed train each way between Winston-Salem and Wadesboro', drop Sunday service and move express to Railway Express trucks; the 1932 express-office order says exclusive passenger-train service 'was discontinued'. A mixed train is passenger service under Rule 1. The 1933 statute gave the Commission power to allow removal (Roanoke Rapids Herald 15 Jun 1933: leave granted 'to remove its one round-trip passenger train from Winston-Salem to Wadesboro') and the last passenger operation was 8 Jul 1933 (frograil after Miller & Vaughn). NCC returns: 2,652 revenue passengers in 1932, 203 in 1933. Freight continued and still does (now Norfolk Southern / CSX jointly) - context only, not drawn. headway_min is an estimate (Rule 3): 1440 = one round trip a day, the single mixed train each way ordered in Docket 7181. Fowler's mileposts put Whitney at 48.6 mi from Winston-Salem Union Station.
sources: Segment-level: 1932 mixed-train order from NCC Docket 7181 and the express-office order No. 7346, and Henderson Daily Dispatch 19 Jul 1932; end 8 Jul 1933 from frograil (Miller & Vaughn), corroborated by Roanoke Rapids Herald 15 Jun 1933 and the NCC 1932-33 return (203 passengers) - as quoted in research/branches/winston_salem_southbound_railway.txt (researched 2026-11-05); the tracer did not re-open these pages. Headway is an estimate from the one-mixed-train-each-way order.

properties.geometry_quality: Whitney - Albemarle: traced 10.3 mi (10.1 WSSB-tagged, 0.2 untagged) against a documented 10.3 mi (Fowler mp 48.6 - 58.9) - exact. Albemarle - Wadesboro: traced 29.3 mi, all on WSSB-tagged ways, against a documented 31.1 mi (Fowler mp 58.9 - 90.0) - 5.8% short. Whole feature 39.8 mi (including the 0.4 km join) vs 41.4 mi. No approximated (straight-line) legs; the two traced legs are joined at Albemarle by a 0.4 km on-track step. Waypoints: Whitney (hamlet), Albemarle (Nominatim city, 0.3-0.4 km), Porter (hamlet), Norwood (town, 1.2 km), Cedar Hill (hamlet), Ansonville (town), Pinkston (hamlet), and the south end of WSSB-tagged track at Wadesboro (hand-pinned, -80.0543, 34.9665: the abandoned WSSB way past the Seaboard/CSX Monroe Subdivision crossing, toward the former ACL connection). WADESBORO END: Wadesboro's passenger depot was not located; the line stops about 2 km east of the town centre geocode, which likely accounts for part of the shortfall. The abandoned way tagged WSSB that continues SE from there toward Cheraw (OSM 169458719) is not drawn (outside the WSSB's 90.0 mi; likely the ACL line). The trace stays on the WSSB at Albemarle and Norwood: 0 mi on the parallel original Norfolk Southern (old_railway_operator=NS) or Yadkin Railroad (Southern) tracks. ERA CAVEAT: drawn on the present OSM alignment; no relocation south of Whitney is known, but this was not checked.

segments.note: Winston-Salem Southbound passenger trains south of Whitney: Whitney - Palestine - Albemarle (regular Winston-Salem - Albemarle service from 13 Feb 1911) - Porter - Norwood - Cedar Hill - Ansonville - Pinkston - Wadesboro (regular Winston-Salem - Wadesboro service from 3 Mar 1911; wvncrails). Drawn from 1911, not 1910: the only 1910 passenger movement south of Whitney was the one-off inaugural special of 24/25 Nov 1910 carrying officials and dignitaries, which the report collapses out (drawable 1911-1933). At Albemarle the WSSB met the Yadkin Railroad and the original Norfolk Southern's Raleigh - Charlotte line; at Norwood the same two; at Wadesboro the Seaboard and the ACL. Through cars Winston-Salem - Florence SC ran from 1 May 1911, the ACL taking over at Wadesboro (that part belongs to the ACL, not drawn here). Fowler marks Hearne (mp 63.3) 'b pass?' - whether it was a passenger stop is open. headway_min 720 is an estimate (Rule 3) from the 1917 count of 4 trains a day the length of the line; other years' train counts not established. Ends 1931 because from mid-1932 only a mixed train ran (next segment).
sources: Segment-level: start 13 Feb 1911 (Albemarle) and 3 Mar 1911 (Wadesboro) from wvncrails, with frograil (Miller & Vaughn) for 13 Feb 1911 regular Stanly County service and the 1917 train count; Florence through cars 1 May 1911 from wvncrails - as quoted in research/branches/winston_salem_southbound_railway.txt (researched 2026-11-05); the tracer did not re-open these pages. segments.note: [OPEN] at BOTH ends. Winston-Salem Southbound shuttle trains Whitney - Badin over Yadkin Railroad (Southern) track operated jointly with the WSSB (5.03 mi 'operated jointly by Southern Railway and Winston-Salem Southbound' in the Yadkin's 1928-29 NCC return; the track was later leased from Alcoa). Badin was the company town of Southern Aluminum / Tallassee Power (Alcoa), built c.1913-17. frograil after Miller & Vaughn: in 1917 there were '10 WSSB passenger trains a day ... 4 going the length of the WSSB, and 6 shuttling between Whitney and Badin', and 'by 1924, a railroad motor car replaced passenger trains on the Whitney to Badin run'; Fowler tags Badin 'b' (1923 Official Guide) under the WSSB. Service is confirmed in 1917, 1923 and 1924 only. 1917 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start - a 1916 Yadkin-WSSB joint-operation contract is reported second-hand, not read. 1924 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when the shuttle stopped; it cannot have outlasted the end of all WSSB passenger operation on 8 Jul 1933, and the Commission's 1932 mixed-train order does not mention Badin, but that silence proves nothing. Do not extend either end without evidence. Whether the Yadkin also ran Badin passenger trains is not established. headway_min 320 is an estimate (Rule 3): 6 shuttle movements a day in 1917 read as 3 each way over a ~16-hour day; the motor-car frequency from c.1924 is unknown. Today the Whitney - Badin track is freight only (the 'Alcoa Spur') - context, not drawn.
sources: Segment-level: 1917 and 1924 from frograil after Miller & Vaughn; 1923 from Fowler's NC table (Badin 'b' = 1923 Official Guide); joint 5.03 mi from the NCC Report 1929-30 Yadkin RR road-operated table - as quoted in research/branches/winston_salem_southbound_railway.txt (researched 2026-11-05); the tracer did not re-open these pages. Both ends [OPEN]; headway is an estimate.
